definitions.explanation: A book used alongside the main textbook in school education to provide additional material or different perspectives on a subject. Often produced by local governments or educational boards.

examples.japanese: {副読本|ふくどくほん}を{配布|はいふ}する。
{道徳|どうとく}の{授業|じゅぎょう}で{副読本|ふくどくほん}を{使|つか}った。
examples.english: We used a supplementary reader in the moral education class.

examples.japanese: {市|し}が{作成|さくせい}した{防災|ぼうさい}の{副読本|ふくどくほん}が{全校|ぜんこう}に{配|くば}られた。
examples.english: A disaster-preparedness supplementary reader created by the city was distributed to all schools.

notes:
{副読本|ふくどくほん} is a supplementary textbook used alongside the main textbook ({教科書|きょうかしょ}) in Japanese schools, primarily at the elementary and junior high school level.

KEY DIFFERENCE FROM {教科書|きょうかしょ}:
- {教科書|きょうかしょ} requires {文部科学省|もんぶかがくしょう} (Ministry of Education) approval
- {副読本|ふくどくほん} does not require ministry approval and is often created by local municipalities or educational boards

COMMON SUBJECTS:
- {道徳|どうとく} (moral education)
- {郷土|きょうど}{学習|がくしゅう} (local studies)
- {防災|ぼうさい} (disaster preparedness)
- {環境|かんきょう}{教育|きょういく} (environmental education)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {副読本|ふくどくほん}を{配布|はいふ}する (distribute supplementary readers)
- {副読本|ふくどくほん}を{使|つか}う (use a supplementary reader)
- {副読本|ふくどくほん}を{作成|さくせい}する (create a supplementary reader)
